content.introduction: The Federal Reserve decided to hold interest rates steady in a 9-3 vote, with three officials dissenting in favor of a rate increase. This decision reflects ongoing debate about inflation and economic outlook. For more details, refer to the official Fed statement.
body:
• Today’s cliffhanger stems from the fact that central bankers are confronting an economic outlook clouded by persistent inflation, conflicting labor market signals and the fallout from the war with Iran.

• Policymakers must decide whether inflation risks have become great enough to warrant a rate hike or whether holding rates steady is the better course until the economic outlook becomes clearer. [...] A couple watch oil tankers, general cargo ships, bulk carriers, and fishing boats anchored in the waters off Muscat near the Strait of Hormuz on June 18, 2026 in Muscat, Oman.

Inflation pressures are building, forcing the Federal Reserve to consider raising interest rates for the first time in three years. [...] However, there is a 36% chance of the first rate hike in three years.

The suspense reflects the raging debate on Wall Street over how new Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh will fight inflation. Warsh has talked tough, but will he act tough? Time will tell.

Not only that, but Warsh has been somewhat cryptic about his plans, arguing it’s not wise to spoon-feed investors with forward guidance on rates.

Four FOMC members dissented from the Fed's statement, with Fed Governor Stephen Miran voting in favor of a 0.25 percentage-point cut. Three other members supported maintaining the current rate, but opposed wording in the statement that signaled a bias toward lowering rates. [...] "The FOMC met expectations and held rates steady today," said Atsi Sheth, chief credit officer at Moody's Ratings, in an email. "As the effects of the Middle East conflict become more pronounced, the case for maintaining policy rates rests on rising inflation risks, while risks to U.S. growth appear contained for now."

In its statement, the FOMC reiterated its goal of achieving a 2% annual inflation rate. The Consumer Price Index stood at 3.3% in March. [...] Kevin Warsh, Mr. Trump's nominee to replace Powell after his term as chair ends on May 15, will inherit a Federal Reserve facing pressures ranging from Mr. Trump's repeated demands for lower interest rates to an inflation reading that jumped last month to its highest level in almost two years. Because interest rate cuts can spur inflation, many economists now predict the Fed will hold off on reductions until later in 2026 or even 2027.

By

Listen

(2 min)

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh testifies at a Senate committee hearing.

WASHINGTON—Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday over the objections of three bank presidents who wanted an increase, underscoring how pressure is building inside the central bank to act on inflation that has run above its target for five years. [...] The Fed held its benchmark rate steady, in a range of 3.5% to 3.75%, in a 9-3 vote. The rate-setting panel issued the same policy statement as it did in June, when it also held rates steady. The decision left Chairman Kevin Warsh’s vow to end the run of above-target inflation to rest for a second straight meeting on words rather than action.
